adviceCardHealth: Keep the pig's skin clean and dry. Provide clean water and balanced nutrition. Monitor regularly for any changes.
adviceCardExudative: Exudative Epidermitis (Greasy Pig Disease) is a bacterial infection causing greasy skin and fever. It spreads through contact with infected pigs or contaminated environments.
adviceCardExudativeDo: Isolate the sick pig immediately. Provide clean, dry bedding. Separate tools and equipment. Contact a veterinarian if symptoms worsen.
adviceCardMange: Sarcoptic Mange is caused by mites burrowing into the skin, causing severe itching and hair loss. It spreads rapidly through direct contact.
adviceCardMangeDo: Isolate the affected pig. Treat the pen with appropriate acaricides. Clean and disinfect all equipment. Wear gloves when handling affected pigs.
adviceCardPox: Swine Pox is a viral disease causing blisters and pustules on the skin. It spreads through mosquitoes and direct contact.
adviceCardPoxDo: Isolate the affected pig. Keep the pen clean and dry. Control mosquito populations. Monitor for secondary bacterial infections.
adviceCardPoxWarning: Call a vet if blisters spread, if the pig stops eating, or if fever develops.
